title: Loose Rein reviews.yaml
description: Which reviews this repository runs, stage by stage: each drafting stage before the mandate, each task as it is built, and the whole change before acceptance. Every stage has the same two parts: what belongs to it alone, switched on or off, and the reviews added to it. Where a review is added is what it reads. Nothing is required: what was not read is named as not read where it is decided on. Outside the mandate's freeze on purpose — which reading the work gets is inside what the mandate delegates, not part of what it decides — and written only by `rein reviews apply` at a terminal or by the dashboard's write session, each change recorded in the audit chain with the whole document it wrote, which is what the file on disk is checked against.

requirements.description: A drafting stage, read before the mandate. `adversarial`: the fresh-context adversarial review of this stage's document, working through the lenses the mandate froze; switched off, the mandate's approval screen names the stage. `reviews` are read over the same document, and their findings go back to the drafter like the adversarial review's.

reviews.description: The reviews added at this stage, in the order a reviewer is asked them: `adversarial`, `correctness`, `simplification`, `security`, or the name of an entry under `custom`. One reviewer launch reads for all of them.

build.description: Each task, read once its change passes the quality gate and before it merges. A finding is sent back to the implementer, as many times as `review_policy.repair_rounds` allows, and a `question` reaches acceptance. Empty: no reviewer reads a task.

reviews.description: The reviews added at this stage, in the order a reviewer is asked them: `adversarial`, `correctness`, `simplification`, `security`, or the name of an entry under `custom`. One reviewer launch reads for all of them.

acceptance.description: The whole change, read once every task has merged. `actual_extraction`: the code is read blind, without the plan, for what it does. `comparison`: that Actual is held against the mandate's claims, so it needs `actual_extraction` on; off, every claim reaches acceptance as `unknown`, a decision card for a person. `reviews` read the whole change, and their findings are the loop's to repair; a blocking finding an earlier reading recorded stands until its anchored code is gone or a human disputes it, whether or not the review is still added. Acceptance says what was not read.

reviews.description: The reviews added at this stage, in the order a reviewer is asked them: `adversarial`, `correctness`, `simplification`, `security`, or the name of an entry under `custom`. One reviewer launch reads for all of them.

custom.description: Reviews beyond the packaged four: a name, and the question the reviewer reads for. The question is held here rather than in a file of its own so that what a review asks is written by the same person, through the same path, and bound by the same record as where it runs.
